newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat Auto in profit in 1st nine months '96.
newsitem.headline: Fiat Auto in profit in 1st nine months '96.

text.p: Italian carmaker Fiat Auto said it remained profitable in the first nine months of 1996 despite difficult markets, expecially its domestic car market, said Fiat Auto managing director Roberto Testore.

"The profitability of the cars division is moving in line with the rest of the group. In the nine months, Fiat Auto stayed in the black and is progressing along its own path," Tessore said while he was attending an Alfa Romeo conference in this north-western Italian town.
On Monday, Fiat said its pretax profits for the first nine months of 1996 fell 36 percent to 1.759 trillion lire on sales up four percent to 57.918 trillion lire.

In 1997, Fiat Auto forecast it will produce 2.5 million cars in the world, helped by its new Palio "world car" which started production in April this year in Brazil, with sales to be extended to many world markets outside Europe.
Italian car production will remain at least 1.5 million cars per year for 1997, similar to that in 1996.
The group's annual production capacity in Italy is 1.8 million. Tessore added, "We always hope for a recovery in the market" to allow a greater utilisation.
